# Requirement #2283: Generator must emit a formatter for a closed generic struct from a referenced assembly

Source: https://github.com/MessagePack-CSharp/MessagePack-CSharp/issues/2283

#### Bug description

`MessagePackGenerator` no longer crashes with `IndexOutOfRangeException` when a `[MessagePackObject]` type has a member whose type is a **closed generic value type defined in a referenced assembly**, but it still does not generate a formatter for that closed generic value type. The compiling assembly gets a resolver, yet the resolver omits `Item<int>`, so trimmed and NativeAOT apps fail at runtime unless the user hand-writes a formatter. The generator must treat the closed generic value type as a first-class serializable type and emit a formatter for it in the consuming assembly.

#### Repro steps

Two projects. `lib`:

```csharp
using MessagePack;
namespace Lib;

[MessagePackObject]
public partial record struct Item<T>([property: Key(0)] string Key);
```

`app`, with a `ProjectReference` to `lib`:

```csharp
using MessagePack; using Lib;
namespace App;

[MessagePackObject]
public sealed partial record Cmd([property: Key(0)] string Scope)
{
    [Key(1)] public Item<int> Member { get; init; }
}
```

Then `dotnet build` on `app`. Both projects are in the attached `mp-repro.zip`.

#### Expected behavior

A clean build, with a generated resolver in `app` that includes a generated formatter for `Item<int>` (for example, `ItemFormatter<int>` or an equivalent closed formatter). No hand-written `[MessagePackFormatter]` should be required on `Item<T>`.

#### Actual behavior

The build succeeds and `app.dll` contains a `GeneratedMessagePackResolver`, but the resolver has no formatter for `Item<int>`. Serializing `Cmd` fails at runtime with a missing formatter error.

- Version used: MessagePack 3.1.8
- Runtime: .NET 10 (SDK 10.0.204), Windows 11

#### Additional context

**What triggers it.** `Item` is declared in `lib`, `Cmd` in `app`:

| `Item` declared as | result |
|---|---|
| `record struct Item<T>` | **no formatter generated** |
| `struct Item<T>` | **no formatter generated** |
| `struct Item` | ok |
| `record struct Item` | ok |
| `class Item<T>` | ok |
| `record class Item<T>` | ok |

So it needs all three of: **generic**, **value type**, **from a referenced assembly**. Moving the identical `Item<T>` declaration into `app` itself makes the formatter generate correctly, which is what makes this specific to metadata symbols.

**Workaround.** Putting `[MessagePackFormatter(typeof(ItemFormatter<>))]` on the generic value type works, at the cost of hand-writing the formatter. The requirement is that this workaround must not be necessary.

**Possibly related:** #2092 reports CS8785 from the v3 generator, but with a different inner exception and no repro.

requirement_points.text: For a [MessagePackObject] type in the compiling assembly that has a member whose type is a closed generic value type declared in a referenced assembly, the source generator completes without throwing IndexOutOfRangeException and does not emit CS8785.
For the same scenario, the MsgPack00xMessagePackAnalyzer completes without throwing IndexOutOfRangeException and does not emit AD0001.
The compiling assembly receives a generated MessagePack resolver that includes the [MessagePackObject] type.
The generated resolver contains a formatter entry for the closed generic value type member (e.g., Item<int>), so the member is covered by the resolver.

plants.description: The location guard around the analyzer reporter is dropped, so diagnostics whose location is not part of the compilation being analyzed (metadata symbols have no source location) are now reported and the analyzer driver throws AD0001.

This Diagnostic.Create is evaluated unconditionally (its result is stored in a local before the reporter is consulted), so indexing DeclaringSyntaxReferences[0] throws IndexOutOfRangeException during the generator run as well, yielding CS8785 and no resolver.

The null-safe GetPropertyIdentifierLocation helper is bypassed and DeclaringSyntaxReferences is indexed directly, so a member whose type comes from metadata (no syntax) throws IndexOutOfRangeException in the analyzer and produces AD0001.
Explicit delegate creation instead of a lambda conversion; identical behaviour.
Renames the helper's parameter from property to symbol (and its doc tag); no behavioural change.
Renames the local callback parameter report to reportAction; no behavioural change.

Only the IsInSource half of the guard is kept; the ContainsSyntaxTree check is gone, so a symbol that originates from another compilation (project reference) still has syntax references in that compilation's trees and the analyzer now reports a location outside the current compilation, which the driver rejects with AD0001.

The reporter is no longer null when running inside the source generator, so the generator now invokes the callback and dereferences the (null) analyzer reporter for any in-source diagnostic, aborting the generator with CS8785.
The null-returning location helper is replaced by First(), which throws InvalidOperationException for members declared in metadata; the analyzer no longer completes cleanly and emits AD0001.

Using the null-forgiving operator instead of the null-conditional removes the tolerance for metadata members; the resulting NullReferenceException aborts the generator, so the compiling assembly gets no generated resolver at all.
